topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, welcome, and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional modalities: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the mechanisms, clinical applications, and major limitations of traditional cancer treatment strategies.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities in signaling, checkpoints, and DNA repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore approaches that exploit specific biological vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, defective cell cycle checkpoints, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, resistance mechanisms, and drug addiction
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the concept of oncogene addiction and the use of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, detailing mechanisms of acquired resistance and therapeutic strategies like drug holidays.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how engineered antibodies and antibody-toxin conjugates are used to target surface proteins on cancer cells.

topics.label: Tumor immunology and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the evidence for cancer immune surveillance and the development of immunotherapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, historical trends, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical survival trends, ongoing clinical challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, and future directions and ethical dilemmas in cancer management.
